correctness.rationale: The proof reconstructs all quantifiers of the source problem. For distinct weights, a generic diagonal input gives six simple linear eigenvalue branches; the symmetric-eigenvalue second-derivative formula forces simultaneous diagonalization on the diagonal subspace. Off-diagonal perturbations then give rational pole identities whose distinct permutahedron rays force transposition-only couplings. Parity makes the cubic trace vanish on zero-diagonal inputs, yielding the exact arithmetic-progression condition on the weight. The sole normalized remaining case (1,0,-1) would force a cubic discriminant to be a polynomial square, contradicted after setting z=0. Repeated-coordinate weights have an explicit direct-sum construction. The checker corroborates the algebraic identities but is not treated as an infinite proof.
